Subject: MAP kickoff + perf plan for streaming chat/TTFT (Acme Health)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I’m attaching a short mutual action plan (MAP_AcmeHealth_v1.3.pdf) that lays out milestones we need to get you from PoC to production. One of Acme’s key gating criteria is predictable streaming latency (TTFT + steady-state token latencies) at the expected concurrency profile — we captured that in the MAP as the performance acceptance criteria.

High-level plan items I pulled into the MAP:
- PoC: sandbox access + 2-week eval with Acme prompt set (Redwood dedicated test pool)
- Perf validation: Redwood will run TTFT + streaming latency benchmarks across target concurrency points and provide p50/p95/p99 numbers, plus throughput (tokens/sec) curves
- Security/Procurement: SOC2 package + contract review (loops to procurement)
- Go/no-go: Acme provides sign-off on perf thresholds and SLA targets

Next steps I propose: I’ll kick off the perf run with our runtime team and share a concise benchmarking report here next week. Can you confirm the target concurrency envelope you care about (typical concurrent users, peak concurrency)? We used the numbers you mentioned (avg 8 concurrent sessions with peaks up to 64) in the MAP draft.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes

Marissa / Vanessa —

Forwarding Priya’s note — they asked for a perf matrix at concurrency points 1, 8, 16, 64 with TTFT and streaming token latency (p50/p95/p99) plus sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for our recommended model variant. Can you run the Redwood dry-run in our dedicated test pool and capture:
- Environment: c6g-gpu-48 (internal test pool) and q4_ig+16 quantized checkpoint (the model we recommended in the MAP)
- Prompts: Acme seed prompt set (drive link in MAP) — run 1k representative prompts, variable lengths (avg 450 tokens).
- Metrics to capture: TTFT (time to first token), per-token streaming latency distribution (p50/p95/p99 for subsequent tokens), overall throughput (tokens/sec) at each concurrency point, observed CPU/GPU utilization, and any K/V cache hit benefits.

Please attach raw logs and a short one-page summary we can share with Priya. Timing: can you run this and post results by EOD Tue Dec 1? I’ll consolidate and send to Acme.

Thanks — Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP kickoff + perf plan — run perf for Acme (requested concurrency points)

Rafael / Vanessa —

Summary of runs (attached: bench-logs-acme-20261201.zip). Short summary below for the MAP deliverable. All numbers are median over 1k prompts per concurrency point unless noted. Test environment notes: dedicated test pool, single model variant (q4_ig+16), auto-batching enabled, KV prefix cache warmed for repeated prompt prefixes where applicable.

Key results (TTFT = time-to-first-token for streaming start):
- Concurrency 1:
  - TTFT p50: 42 ms, p95: 95 ms, p99: 160 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency (subsequent tokens) p50/p95/p99: 7 ms / 18 ms / 48 ms
  - Throughput: sustained ~1,250 tokens/sec (single session streaming)

- Concurrency 8:
  - TTFT p50: 45 ms, p95: 115 ms, p99: 210 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50/p95/p99: 8 ms / 22 ms / 55 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~9,400 tokens/sec across 8 sessions (approx 1,175 tokens/sec/session)

- Concurrency 16:
  - TTFT p50: 48 ms, p95: 140 ms, p99: 260 ms
  - Streaming per-token latency p50/p95/p99: 9 ms / 25 ms / 70 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~17,600 tokens/sec (~1,100 tokens/sec/session)

- Concurrency 64 (sustained burst, 5-minute window):
  - TTFT p50: 65 ms, p95: 320 ms, p99: 720 ms (note: tail increased during sustained 5-minute burst; see mitigation notes)
  - Streaming per-token latency p50/p95/p99: 12 ms / 45 ms / 180 ms
  - Aggregate throughput: ~58k tokens/sec (approx 900 tokens/sec/session average under heavy contention)

Observations / recommendations:
- At typical steady concurrency (8–16) we meet the p95 < 200 ms TTFT requirement Priya mentioned. p99 tails are sensitive to burst patterns and KV cache cold starts.
- For heavy sustained bursts (64 concurrent long-lived sessions) we observed a TTFT tail increase due to transient kernel scheduling and buffer contention; adding a small burst buffer (reserve capacity) or per-tenant prioritized slots in the routing policy reduces p99 by ~40% in repeat tests.
- Auto-batching gave good throughput without materially hurting p50 TTFT; if Acme prefers stricter p95 tail targets we can disable batching for critical routes at the cost of ~10–15% throughput.

Attached: one-page summary (inside bench-logs zip) + raw logs. Let me know if you want a deeper breakdown by average prompt length bucket.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: bench-logs-acme-20261201.zip

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme MAP perf deliverable & close play (summary + next steps)

Priya —

Thanks for confirming the concurrency envelope. Please find the perf summary from our run below (attached full logs and MAP edition v1.3). Short version for your review:

- Acceptance: For the recommended model/quantization we meet your p95 TTFT target (<200 ms) at steady concurrency profiles (1, 8, 16).
- Tail guidance: p99 during sustained 64-concurrency bursts exceeded 200 ms in our first run; we have two mitigation paths: add reserved burst capacity (recommended for telehealth peaks) or apply per-route prioritized slots (software policy) — both reduce p99 by ~30–45% in follow-ups.

Selected numbers (from runs):
- TTFT p50/p95/p99 at concurrency 8: 45 ms / 115 ms / 210 ms
- Streaming per-token p50/p95/p99 at concurrency 8: 8 ms / 22 ms / 55 ms
- Throughput: ~9.4k tokens/sec aggregate at concurrency 8 (~1.2k/session)

Next steps and timeline (MAP-aligned):
1) You review the MAP and perf summary (this week).
2) If acceptable, procurement routes contract draft; Redwood will reserve a small burst buffer for Acme during the first 90 days of Dedicated usage (if contract signs) — Rafael to coordinate.
3) Optional: run a follow-up targeted burst test with reserved buffer enabled (2–3 days) to demonstrate improved p99; engineering (Marissa) can drop-in that run on request.

Action items for Acme: please confirm whether you want Redwood to run the reserved-buffer test (we’ll schedule it within 48 hours) and whether the MAP incremental milestone dates look OK.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
